note: Exterior kits: what stands on the ground at a key location, arranged by rule. Parts are shared across archetypes so a rubble pile is one identity everywhere. A kit resolves per archetype, falling back to its family, so every archetype has one. Arrangement decides the shape - a stone circle is a ring, a mine head terraces down the fall of the slope, a monastery is a courtyard, a cave is a mouth with its approach. Plot and dimension metres are schematic placeholders sized for legibility, not measured art. Parts that move the ground carry a `shaping` spec; the planner emits those both as parametric primitives, which are the truth, and as a sampled surface grid, which is the coarse derived form.
